title: 527.  Beethoven: Napoleon and the Music of War LIVE at the Royal Albert Hall

sentences.en: Hello, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Happy New Year and welcome back to the recording of the live show that Dominic and I did at the Royal Albert Hall on the 18th of October.
sentences.zh: 新年快乐，欢迎回到我们10月18日在皇家阿尔伯特音乐厅举办的现场演出录音。

sentences.en: You should already have heard the episode on Mozart.
sentences.zh: 你们应该已经听过关于莫扎特的那一集了。

sentences.en: And now in the second half, we are looking at Beethoven.
sentences.zh: 现在下半场，我们要讲的是贝多芬。

sentences.en: I hope you enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 希望你们喜欢。

sentences.en: Welcome back, everybody.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回来，各位。

sentences.en: Always start second half with a banger, they say.
sentences.zh: 俗话说，下半场开场总得来点震撼的。

sentences.en: And that, of course, was the banger to end all bangers.
sentences.zh: 而刚才那段，当然就是震撼之中的震撼。

sentences.en: The first movement of Beethoven's Fifth Symphony
sentences.zh: 贝多芬《第五交响曲》的第一乐章，

sentences.en: premiered in December 1808 in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 于1808年12月在维也纳首演。

sentences.en: And Dominic, the opening of that movement must be the most famous opening to any piece of music ever written, I'd have thought.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我想那个乐章的开头，一定是史上最著名的音乐开场了吧。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: So we have had Mozart and the second half is about a very different character, someone who is brooding, unfriendly, difficult.
sentences.zh: 我们讲完了莫扎特，下半场要讲的是一个性格迥异的人物，一个阴郁、不友善、难以相处的人。

sentences.en: And here he is to talk about Ludwig van Beethoven.
sentences.zh: 现在，有请他来聊聊路德维希·凡·贝多芬。
zh_words: 聊聊路德维希·凡·贝多芬

sentences.en: Dominic, take it away.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，请开始你的讲述。

sentences.en: When I wrote that joke, I knew you would laugh.
sentences.zh: 写那个笑话的时候，我就知道你会笑。

sentences.en: So, Tom, you ended with Mozart's death and funeral in 1791.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，你刚才讲到了莫扎特1791年的去世和葬礼。

sentences.en: No great send-off, a slightly lacklustre occasion.
sentences.zh: 没有隆重的送别，场面略显冷清。

sentences.en: And let's start by fast-forwarding three decades to March 1827, to the death and funeral of his great successor, Ludwig van Beethoven.
sentences.zh: 让我们把时间快进三十年，来到1827年3月，看看他伟大的继任者路德维希·凡·贝多芬的去世和葬礼。

sentences.en: And it's a completely different scene.
sentences.zh: 那完全是另一番景象。

sentences.en: As Beethoven lies dying, also in Vienna, presents, cash, cakes are coming in from all over Europe.
sentences.zh: 当贝多芬在维也纳弥留之际，来自欧洲各地的礼物、现金和蛋糕源源不断地送来。

sentences.en: Beethoven's last recorded words, greet the arrival from Mainz of a case of his favourite Rhineland wine.
sentences.zh: 贝多芬留下的最后记录，是迎接从美因茨运来的一箱他最爱的莱茵葡萄酒。

sentences.en: And his last words were, pity, pity, too late.
sentences.zh: 他留下的遗言是：可惜，可惜，太晚了。

sentences.en: And then he died.
sentences.zh: 然后他就去世了。

sentences.en: And when he did die, on the evening of the 26th of March, it was the news story of the year.
sentences.zh: 当他在3月26日傍晚去世时，这成了当年的头条新闻。

sentences.en: So when they held the funeral three days later, crowds had gathered outside Beethoven's apartment.
sentences.zh: 所以三天后举行葬礼时，贝多芬的公寓外已经聚集了人群。

sentences.en: There was a choir outside to see him off.
sentences.zh: 外面有唱诗班为他送行。

sentences.en: The schools were all given the day off.
sentences.zh: 所有的学校都放假一天。

sentences.en: On the way to the church and then to the cemetery, the crowds were so thick, it took them ages to pass through.
sentences.zh: 在前往教堂和墓地的路上，人群拥挤不堪，队伍走了好久才通过。

sentences.en: And all the way, some of the best-known people in Vienna were holding a kind of torch-lit parade, most famously the young composer Franz Schubert.
sentences.zh: 一路上，维也纳一些最知名的人物举着火把游行，其中最著名的是年轻的作曲家弗朗茨·舒伯特。

sentences.en: So clearly something had changed since the death of Mozart.
sentences.zh: 显然，自莫扎特去世以来，情况已经发生了变化。

sentences.en: And a lot of that has to do with
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上要归功于

sentences.en: Beethoven himself.
sentences.zh: 贝多芬本人。

sentences.en: So many of you, I guess, will already have an idea of Beethoven in your mind.
sentences.zh: 我想你们很多人心中已经有了贝多芬的形象。

sentences.en: The wild hair, the ferocious, frowning expression, the unkempt appearance, the papers falling from his pocket.
sentences.zh: 狂乱的头发，凶狠皱眉的表情，不修边幅的外表，口袋里掉出来的纸张。

sentences.en: An intellectual, an artiSt. Mozart is fun and Beethoven is serious.
sentences.zh: 一位知识分子，一位艺术家。莫扎特代表快乐，而贝多芬代表严肃。

sentences.en: That's the stereotype.
sentences.zh: 这就是刻板印象。

sentences.en: And I think this is really important because I think it is Beethoven, more than anybody else,
sentences.zh: 我认为这一点非常重要，因为我觉得正是贝多芬，比任何人都更早地

sentences.en: who invents this idea of the creator, the artistic genius, as a lonely, difficult, unhappy, but brilliant man.
sentences.zh: 创造了这种创作者、艺术天才的形象：一个孤独、难以相处、不快乐但才华横溢的人。

sentences.en: A bit like Tom.
sentences.zh: 有点像汤姆。

sentences.en: Now, one difference between Beethoven and Mozart, obviously, is that
sentences.zh: 现在，贝多芬和莫扎特之间的一个区别显而易见，那就是

sentences.en: Beethoven is not Austrian.
sentences.zh: 贝多芬不是奥地利人。

sentences.en: Beethoven is German.
sentences.zh: 贝多芬是德国人。

sentences.en: He was born in Bonn in the west of Germany in December
sentences.zh: 他于1770年12月出生在德国西部的波恩。

sentences.en: Bonn was a small town that belonged to the electorate of Cologne.
sentences.zh: 波恩是一个属于科隆选侯国的小镇。

sentences.en: And music was the family business.
sentences.zh: 音乐是他们家的家族事业。

sentences.en: Beethoven's father was a singer, but his alcoholism stymied his career.
sentences.zh: 贝多芬的父亲是一名歌手，但他的酗酒毁了他的职业生涯。

sentences.en: Now, as with Mozart, his father pushed him ferociously.
sentences.zh: 和莫扎特一样，他的父亲对他进行了严酷的逼迫。

sentences.en: He started giving him regular keyboard lessons when Ludwig was just five.
sentences.zh: 路德维希才五岁时，他就开始让他进行定期的键盘练习。

sentences.en: He would make him practice until he cried.
sentences.zh: 他会逼他练琴直到哭泣。

sentences.en: He would make him practice until midnight.
sentences.zh: 他会逼他练琴直到午夜。

sentences.en: And he would beat him when Ludwig made a mistake.
sentences.zh: 如果路德维希弹错，他就会打他。

sentences.en: And did it work?
sentences.zh: 这奏效了吗？

sentences.en: Did it?
sentences.zh: 奏效了吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: It didn't.
sentences.zh: 没有奏效。

sentences.en: Because although Ludwig was clearly very good, he wasn't a prodigy on the scale of Mozart.
sentences.zh: 因为虽然路德维希显然非常优秀，但他并不是莫扎特那种级别的神童。

sentences.en: When he reached the age of 10, he was still barely known within his own town.
sentences.zh: 当他十岁时，他在自己的城镇里几乎还是默默无闻。

sentences.en: Nobody effectively had noticed him on a kind of continental scale.
sentences.zh: 实际上，在欧洲大陆的层面上，没人注意到他。

sentences.en: But then, at the age of 11, he got a new piano teacher, a massively important figure in his life, who rejoiced in the name of Christian Goklob Nefer.
sentences.zh: 但后来，在他11岁时，他有了一位新的钢琴老师，一位对他一生至关重要的人物，他有一个响亮的名字：克里斯蒂安·戈特洛布·内弗。
zh_words: 克里斯蒂安·戈特洛布·内弗

sentences.en: And Nefer was a Protestant.
sentences.zh: 内弗是一位新教徒。

sentences.en: The Beethovens were Catholics.
sentences.zh: 而贝多芬一家是天主教徒。

sentences.en: And Nefer was tied in to the Enlightenment.
sentences.zh: 内弗与启蒙运动有着紧密的联系。

sentences.en: So he was full of ideas about reason and virtue and reform, full of the writings of Voltaire and Kant.
sentences.zh: 所以他满脑子都是关于理性、美德和改革的思想，深受伏尔泰和康德著作的影响。

sentences.en: And he passes these on to the young Beethoven.
sentences.zh: 他把这些思想传授给了年轻的贝多芬。

sentences.en: Now, through his
sentences.zh: 现在，通过他的

sentences.en: Enlightenment enthusiasms, Nefer is very well connected.
sentences.zh: 启蒙运动热情，内弗拥有非常广泛的人脉。

sentences.en: And one of his friends is a chap called
sentences.zh: 他的朋友之一是一位名叫

sentences.en: Count Ferdinand Waldstein, who lives in Bonn and is very friendly with the Elector.
sentences.zh: 费迪南德·冯·瓦尔德斯坦伯爵的人，他住在波恩，与选帝侯关系非常亲密。

sentences.en: And it's Waldstein who gets Ludwig a job playing the organ for the Elector.
sentences.zh: 正是瓦尔德斯坦为路德维希争取到了为选帝侯演奏管风琴的工作。

sentences.en: They think this is tremendous.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这太棒了。

sentences.en: They have great ambitions for Ludwig.
sentences.zh: 他们对路德维希寄予厚望。

sentences.en: And in 1787, when he's 16 years old, they sent him to the City of Music to Vienna.
sentences.zh: 1787年，当他16岁时，他们把他送到了音乐之都维也纳。

sentences.en: And there, legend tells, he meets the great man.
sentences.zh: 传说他在那里见到了那位大人物。

sentences.en: He meets Mozart.
sentences.zh: 他见到了莫扎特。

sentences.en: And the story runs that Mozart got him to play the piano.
sentences.zh: 故事说莫扎特让他弹奏钢琴。

sentences.en: Ludwig played, improvising brilliantly.
sentences.zh: 路德维希弹奏了一曲，即兴发挥得非常出色。

sentences.en: And Mozart stood there impassively.
sentences.zh: 莫扎特面无表情地站在那里。

sentences.en: And when the last note died away, Mozart said nothing.
sentences.zh: 当最后一个音符消失时，莫扎特什么也没说。

sentences.en: He just went into the next room where his friends were sitting.
sentences.zh: 他只是走进隔壁朋友们坐着的房间。

sentences.en: And he said to them, keep an eye on that young man.
sentences.zh: 他对他们说：留意那个年轻人。

sentences.en: One day, he will give the world something to talk about.
sentences.zh: 总有一天，他会给世界带来谈资。

sentences.en: And do you think that actually happened?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这事真的发生过吗？

sentences.en: I think that happened.
sentences.zh: 我觉得发生过。

sentences.en: And that's how he spoke.
sentences.zh: 他说话就是那个风格。

sentences.en: That is just how he spoke.
sentences.zh: 他说话就是那样。

sentences.en: Well, maybe it did happen, maybe it didn't.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许发生过，也许没有。

sentences.en: But the fact the story exists at all...
sentences.zh: 但这个故事的存在本身……

sentences.en: Yeah, that's the important thing, right?
sentences.zh: 没错，这才是重点，对吧？

sentences.en: The fact the story exists at all is proof of how desperate people were to see a connection between them.
sentences.zh: 这个故事的存在本身，就证明了人们是多么渴望看到他们两人之间存在某种联系。

sentences.en: But that first trip didn't last long.
sentences.zh: 但那次初访并没有持续太久。

sentences.en: So Beethoven came home after two weeks because his mother was ill.
sentences.zh: 贝多芬两周后就回家了，因为他母亲病了。

sentences.en: But then in the autumn of 1792, he came back to Vienna for good.
sentences.zh: 但在1792年秋天，他永久地回到了维也纳。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because the French Revolution had broken out.
sentences.zh: 因为法国大革命爆发了。

sentences.en: French armies were rampaging across the map of Europe, spreading perturbation and despair.
sentences.zh: 法军在欧洲地图上横冲直撞，散布着动荡与绝望。

sentences.en: The court fled Bonn.
sentences.zh: 宫廷逃离了波恩。

sentences.en: Bonn was no longer safe.
sentences.zh: 波恩不再安全了。

sentences.en: And Beethoven was sent to Vienna.
sentences.zh: 于是贝多芬被送往维也纳。

sentences.en: Now, of course, by this point, Mozart was dead.
sentences.zh: 当然，此时莫扎特已经去世了。

sentences.en: So Beethoven is going to study with that other great Austrian composer,
sentences.zh: 所以贝多芬要去跟随另一位伟大的奥地利作曲家学习，

sentences.en: Josef Haydn.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·海顿。

sentences.en: And before he left, Count Waldstein wrote him a note.
sentences.zh: 在他离开之前，瓦尔德斯坦伯爵给他写了一张便条。

sentences.en: Mozart, he said, is dead.
sentences.zh: 他说，莫扎特死了。

sentences.en: But Mozart's genius is still alive and is in mourning.
sentences.zh: 但莫扎特的天才依然活着，正在哀悼。

sentences.en: And it is waiting for somebody.
sentences.zh: 它在等待某个人。

sentences.en: It is waiting for you.
sentences.zh: 它在等待你。

sentences.en: And from Haydn, you will receive the spirit of Mozart.
sentences.zh: 从海顿那里，你将继承莫扎特的精神。

sentences.en: And so off he goes to Vienna, the city where he will compose his greatest works.
sentences.zh: 于是他前往维也纳，那座他将创作出最伟大作品的城市。

sentences.en: And I think what's so interesting about this is that a bit like Mozart, to begin with, he is better known as a player of music rather than as a composer.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这最有趣的地方在于，就像莫扎特一样，起初他作为演奏家比作为作曲家更出名。

sentences.en: And so since he started out on the piano, let's have one of his very greatest piano pieces.
sentences.zh: 既然他从钢琴起步，那我们就来欣赏他最伟大的钢琴曲之一吧。

sentences.en: And we're going to hear the second movement of the fourth piano concerto, which premiered in 1808 at the same evening that saw the Fifth Symphony premiered.
sentences.zh: 我们要听的是《第四钢琴协奏曲》的第二乐章，它与《第五交响曲》在1808年的同一个晚上首演。

sentences.en: And we are going to hear on the piano, Mishka Rashti Mohamed.
sentences.zh: 钢琴演奏者是米什卡·拉什蒂·穆罕默德。
zh_words: 米什卡·拉什蒂·穆罕默德

sentences.en: Beautifully played.
sentences.zh: 弹得真美。

sentences.en: And on that evening in Vienna, when it was premiered, the piano was played by
sentences.zh: 而在维也纳首演的那个晚上，钢琴是由

sentences.en: Beethoven itself.
sentences.zh: 贝多芬本人演奏的。

sentences.en: And Dominic, we've talked a lot about Vienna over the course of this evening.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，今晚我们聊了很多关于维也纳的话题。

sentences.en: Should we just focus in and describe the capital?
sentences.zh: 我们要不要聚焦一下，描述一下这座首都？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So obviously for Beethoven, Vienna is much more foreign than it is for Mozart.
sentences.zh: 显然，对于贝多芬来说，维也纳比对莫扎特来说要陌生得多。

sentences.en: It's the capital of the Habsburg dynasty.
sentences.zh: 它是哈布斯堡王朝的首都。

sentences.en: It is at this point by far the biggest German speaking city in Europe with about a quarter of a million people.
sentences.zh: 当时它是欧洲最大的德语城市，人口约有二十五万。

sentences.en: So that's twice as big as Berlin.
sentences.zh: 那是柏林人口的两倍。

sentences.en: It's a city at war.
sentences.zh: 这是一座处于战争中的城市。

sentences.en: So from 1792, Austria is at war on and off for the next 22 years or so.
sentences.zh: 从1792年开始，奥地利在接下来的22年左右断断续续地处于战争状态。

sentences.en: It's twice occupied by the French.
sentences.zh: 它曾两次被法国占领。

sentences.en: There are stories about Beethoven literally sheltering under his bedclothes as the shells are kind of raining down overhead.
sentences.zh: 有故事说贝多芬在炮弹如雨点般落下时，真的躲在被子里避难。

sentences.en: And also, of course, for him, it's the city of
sentences.zh: 当然，对他来说，这也是

sentences.en: Mozart.
sentences.zh: 莫扎特的城市。

sentences.en: And when he arrives, Mozart has been dead for a year.
sentences.zh: 当他到达时，莫扎特已经去世一年了。

sentences.en: And people are already saying, who is going to be the next Mozart?
sentences.zh: 人们已经在问，谁会是下一个莫扎特？

sentences.en: You have a sense, I think, that if the next Mozart doesn't exist, they're going to invent him anyway.
sentences.zh: 我想你会有种感觉，如果下一个莫扎特不存在，他们也会把他塑造出来。

sentences.en: And very soon after Beethoven's arrival, they say, call off the search.
sentences.zh: 贝多芬到达后不久，他们就说，不用再找了。

sentences.en: We have found him.
sentences.zh: 我们已经找到了。

sentences.en: In fact, after his first year, his teacher,
sentences.zh: 事实上，在他第一年之后，他的老师，

sentences.en: Josef Haydn, wrote to the elector of Cologne.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·海顿，写信给科隆选帝侯。

sentences.en: And he said, he will be one of the greatest artists in Europe.
sentences.zh: 他说，他将成为欧洲最伟大的艺术家之一。

sentences.en: And I will be proud to call myself his teacher.
sentences.zh: 我很自豪能称自己为他的老师。

sentences.en: And the lovely thing is that is exactly what Tom's teachers used to say about James Holland.
sentences.zh: 可爱的是，这正是汤姆的老师们过去评价詹姆斯·霍兰德的话。

sentences.en: Sorry, Tom.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，汤姆。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: No, I'm used to this.
sentences.zh: 不，我习惯了。

sentences.en: I'm used to it.
sentences.zh: 我习惯了。

sentences.en: You deserved it after that singing.
sentences.zh: 你刚才那段歌唱表演之后，你确实该受点调侃。

sentences.en: Four long years.
sentences.zh: 漫长的四年。

sentences.en: Now, he can't just be Mozart because the context has changed.
sentences.zh: 现在，他不能只是莫扎特，因为背景已经变了。

sentences.en: For example, the way you make music is changing.
sentences.zh: 例如，创作音乐的方式正在改变。

sentences.en: Beethoven literally has different instruments to play with.
sentences.zh: 贝多芬确实有了不同的乐器可以使用。

sentences.en: For example, pianos that have a much greater range and a richer sound.
sentences.zh: 例如，音域更广、音色更丰富的钢琴。

sentences.en: So if you've wondered why Beethoven might sound different from Mozart, that's one of the reasons.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你曾好奇为什么贝多芬听起来和莫扎特不同，这就是原因之一。

sentences.en: But even more importantly, I think, the way you make money from music has changed.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得更重要的是，音乐的获利方式发生了改变。

sentences.en: So until this point, as Tom was describing in the first half, most musicians depended on an aristocratic household.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，正如汤姆在前半部分所描述的那样，大多数音乐家都依赖于贵族家庭。

sentences.en: So Beethoven's teacher, Haydn, depended on the Esterhazy family.
sentences.zh: 所以贝多芬的老师海顿，就依赖于埃斯特哈齐家族。

sentences.en: He lived at the Esterhazy Palace over the border in

sentences.en: That is a passage of music that historians have always been fascinated by because it's conventionally
sentences.zh: 那段音乐一直让历史学家们着迷，因为它通常

sentences.en: seen as providing the kind of the soundtrack to an age of revolution, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 被视为那个革命时代的配乐，不是吗？

sentences.en: And just for those not familiar with the opera, to give a bit of context, it's set in Spain in the 16th century in a prison.
sentences.zh: 对于那些不熟悉这部歌剧的人，我简单介绍一下背景：故事发生在16世纪西班牙的一所监狱里。

sentences.en: And what you've just heard is prisoners emerging from their cells, coming, blinking into the sunlight, singing of the delight they feel at their liberation.
sentences.zh: 你刚才听到的是囚犯们从牢房里走出来，在阳光下眨着眼睛，歌唱着他们重获自由的喜悦。

sentences.en: And so it's always kind of associated with the fall of the Bastille, the overthrowing of monarchical despotism.
sentences.zh: 所以它总是与攻占巴士底狱、推翻君主专制联系在一起。

sentences.en: But Dominic, I mean, as I said, I am familiar with your methods, and I kind of have a hunch that you're going to tell me it's more complicated than that.
sentences.zh: 但是多米尼克，正如我所说，我了解你的套路，我有一种预感，你会告诉我事情远比这复杂。

sentences.en: Surprise, surprise, it's more complicated than that.
sentences.zh: 惊喜吧，事情确实比这复杂。

sentences.en: So Beethoven had been working on Fidelio for years, and he got the idea from a French play about a bloke who's rescued from prison by his wife.
sentences.zh: 贝多芬创作《费德里奥》花了多年时间，灵感来自一部法国戏剧，讲的是一个男人被妻子从监狱里救出来的故事。

sentences.en: But it seems pretty likely that the French play is actually set during the terror, and this bloke may be an aristocrat.
sentences.zh: 但很有可能这部法国戏剧的背景实际上是在恐怖统治时期，而且这个男人可能是一位贵族。

sentences.en: And I think the politics of Fidelio may be a little bit more complicated, more conservative maybe, than people think.
sentences.zh: 我认为《费德里奥》的政治内涵可能比人们想象的要复杂一些，甚至更保守一些。

sentences.en: So remember, this is taking place, this premiere, in Vienna in 1814, in an atmosphere of conservatism, of reaction.
sentences.zh: 记住，这部歌剧于1814年在维也纳首演，当时正处于一种保守、反动的氛围中。

sentences.en: The old order has won.
sentences.zh: 旧秩序已经获胜了。

sentences.en: And at the end of Fidelio, when the hero gets his freedom, he doesn't get it because the mob has stormed the prison, not at all.
sentences.zh: 在《费德里奥》结尾，当英雄获得自由时，并不是因为暴民冲进了监狱，完全不是。

sentences.en: He gets it because of the intervention of the kind-hearted, benevolent governor, effectively the emperor.
sentences.zh: 他获得自由是因为那位心地善良、仁慈的总督——实际上就是皇帝——的干预。

sentences.en: In other words, this is a victory for the old order.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这是旧秩序的胜利。

sentences.en: It's the old order that has prevailed.
sentences.zh: 是旧秩序占据了上风。

sentences.en: And the freedom that the opera is celebrating, Tom, in 1814, those first audiences in Vienna, to them it's freedom from the war, freedom from the tyranny of Napoleon,
sentences.zh: 而这部歌剧所颂扬的自由，汤姆，对于1814年维也纳的首批观众来说，那是摆脱战争的自由，摆脱拿破仑暴政的自由，

sentences.en: freedom from the despotism of the French.
sentences.zh: 摆脱法国人专制的自由。

sentences.en: The despotism of the French.
sentences.zh: 法国人的专制。

sentences.en: We know all about that, don't we?
sentences.zh: 我们对此再了解不过了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because Theo, our beloved producer, is, of course, well, purports to be French.
sentences.zh: 因为西奥，我们敬爱的制作人，当然，嗯，自称是法国人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: But I think there's another aspect of Fidelio that is actually more interesting.
sentences.zh: 但我认为《费德里奥》还有另一个方面其实更有趣。

sentences.en: Some of Beethoven's biographers suggest that this picture, this bloke who's locked up in a prison, cut off from the outside world, is a kind of nightmarish self-portrait.
sentences.zh: 贝多芬的一些传记作者认为，这幅画面——一个被关在监狱里、与世隔绝的男人——是一种噩梦般的自画像。

sentences.en: Because as many of you will know, at the time that Fidelio goes on stage,
sentences.zh: 因为正如你们许多人所知，在《费德里奥》上演时，

sentences.en: Beethoven has been going deaf for probably at least 12 years.
sentences.zh: 贝多芬可能已经失聪至少12年了。

sentences.en: The cruelest punishment possible for a composer.
sentences.zh: 这对作曲家来说是最残酷的惩罚。

sentences.en: Now, his deafness probably started at the end of the 1790s, when he's in his late 20s.
sentences.zh: 他的耳聋可能始于18世纪90年代末，当时他才20多岁。

sentences.en: We don't know really what caused it.
sentences.zh: 我们并不真正知道是什么原因导致的。

sentences.en: We do know that in the summer of 1802, he went to a place called Heiligenstadt for the summer, and he wrote a letter to his brothers,
sentences.zh: 我们确实知道，1802年夏天，他去了一个叫海利根施塔特的地方避暑，并给他的兄弟们写了一封信，

sentences.en: explaining, apologizing for his horrendous form in recent months.
sentences.zh: 解释并为他近几个月来糟糕的状态道歉。

sentences.en: And he said, listen, the truth is, I'm losing my hearing, and that one day I will be cut off from the outside world.
sentences.zh: 他说，听着，事实是我正在失去听力，总有一天我会与世隔绝。

sentences.en: I'll have to live like an exile in my own head.
sentences.zh: 我将不得不像个流亡者一样活在自己的头脑里。

sentences.en: And he says, I've thought about ending it all, about ending this wretched existence, but it was my art that held me back.
sentences.zh: 他说，我曾想过结束这一切，结束这悲惨的存在，但正是我的艺术支撑着我。

sentences.en: It seemed impossible to me to leave this world until I'd written all the works that I was capable of.
sentences.zh: 在我写出我力所能及的所有作品之前，离开这个世界对我来说似乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: And that brings us back to something that's been running through this story from the very beginning of the show, which is the idea of art as something special
sentences.zh: 这让我们回到了从节目一开始就贯穿始终的一个主题，即艺术是一种特殊的东西，

sentences.en: and something sacred, dare I say sacral, Tom.
sentences.zh: 一种神圣的东西，我敢说是神圣的，汤姆。

sentences.en: Go for it.
sentences.zh: 说吧。

sentences.en: It is art that saves us, that gives our lives meaning.
sentences.zh: 是艺术拯救了我们，赋予了我们生命意义。

sentences.en: And this, of course, becomes one of the foundational ideas of Romanticism, the idea that art is the supreme good, the summit of human existence,
sentences.zh: 当然，这成为了浪漫主义的基本思想之一，即艺术是至善，是人类存在的巅峰，

sentences.en: that it is art that makes life worth living.
sentences.zh: 是艺术让生命变得值得活下去。

sentences.en: Now, of course, that's not much consolation to poor Beethoven, who is losing his hearing.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对正在失去听力的可怜的贝多芬来说，并没有多少安慰。

sentences.en: His hearing, in fact, gets worse and worse.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他的听力越来越差。

sentences.en: Because by 1814, the year of Fidelio, if you sit down to listen to something, and it's Ludwig van Beethoven playing the piano, you know you're not in for a brilliant evening,
sentences.zh: 因为到了1814年，《费德里奥》上演的那一年，如果你坐下来听音乐，而弹钢琴的是路德维希·凡·贝多芬，你知道你不会度过一个美妙的夜晚，

sentences.en: because he can't tell if it's been tuned properly, and he also can't tell if he's making mistakes.
sentences.zh: 因为他听不出琴是否调准了，也听不出自己是否弹错了。

sentences.en: So actually, at the end of the year, he gives up playing in public, and at this point, he starts carrying these conversation books.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，在那一年年底，他放弃了公开演奏，从那时起，他开始随身携带这些谈话簿。

sentences.en: So when he meets you in the street, and you're talking to him, you have to write down in the book what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 所以当他在街上遇到你，和你交谈时，你必须在簿子上写下你想说的话。

sentences.en: So, sad to say, by the mid-1810s,
sentences.zh: 所以，遗憾的是，到了19世纪10年代中期，

sentences.en: Beethoven has, to some extent, ended up in that dungeon.
sentences.zh: 贝多芬在某种程度上最终被关进了那个地牢。

sentences.en: Now, he had a very unhappy and lonely love life.
sentences.zh: 此外，他的爱情生活非常不幸且孤独。

sentences.en: Some of you may know that he wrote a letter to a woman that he called his immortal beloved.
sentences.zh: 你们有些人可能知道，他给一个他称之为“永恒的爱人”的女人写过一封信。

sentences.en: It's a great film, Gary Oldman.
sentences.zh: 那部电影很棒，加里·奥德曼演的。

sentences.en: Which is made into a Gary Oldman film, exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是改编成了加里·奥德曼的那部电影，没错。

sentences.en: In which he said, you know, you're the love of my life, but we can never be together.
sentences.zh: 他在信中说，你知道，你是我的挚爱，但我们永远无法在一起。

sentences.en: And we don't really know, again, who that was.
sentences.zh: 而且我们确实不知道那个人到底是谁。

sentences.en: His family life was a nightmare.
sentences.zh: 他的家庭生活是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: For a lot of the 1810s, he's locked in this dreadful custody battle over his nephew, Karl.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪10年代的大部分时间里，他都陷入了与侄子卡尔之间可怕的监护权之争。

sentences.en: In 1820, he turned 50.
And by this point, I think he's a very disconsolate figure, Beethoven.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，我认为贝多芬是一个非常忧郁的人物。

sentences.en: When he goes out, he's very scruffy and distracted.
sentences.zh: 他出门时，显得非常邋遢且心不在焉。

sentences.en: At one point, the Viennese police arrested him for being a tramp.
sentences.zh: 有一次，维也纳警察甚至因为他像个流浪汉而逮捕了他。

sentences.en: And part of the problem, of course, is they're talking to him, and he can't hear what they're saying.
sentences.zh: 当然，部分问题在于警察在和他说话，而他听不见他们在说什么。

sentences.en: It's a bit of a problem.
sentences.zh: 这确实是个问题。

sentences.en: But the weird thing is that all this is actually great news for the Beethoven brand.
sentences.zh: 但奇怪的是，这一切对“贝多芬”这个品牌来说其实是个好消息。

sentences.en: Because it perfectly captures the ethos of the Romantic age.
sentences.zh: 因为它完美地捕捉到了浪漫主义时代的精神。

sentences.en: The idea of a lonely hero who is battling with his demons in a kind of spiritual exile.
sentences.zh: 一个孤独的英雄在某种精神流亡中与心魔搏斗的形象。

sentences.en: Now, all the time,
sentences.zh: 然而，一直以来，

sentences.en: Beethoven is still making music.
sentences.zh: 贝多芬仍在创作音乐。

sentences.en: He is making music that is more demanding, more challenging than ever before.
sentences.zh: 他创作的音乐比以往任何时候都更具挑战性，要求更高。

sentences.en: Some people say it's too challenging.
sentences.zh: 有些人说这太难了。

sentences.en: So you have a sense of an emerging breach between the masses, who like the kind of fun, easy operas that are coming from Italy, and the connoisseurs,
sentences.zh: 所以你会感觉到大众——他们喜欢意大利那种有趣、轻松的歌剧——与鉴赏家之间出现了裂痕，

sentences.en: who think that if it's difficult, that means it must be profound.
sentences.zh: 鉴赏家们认为，如果作品很难，那就意味着它一定很深刻。

sentences.en: And Beethoven himself was in no doubt about who he was writing for.
sentences.zh: 而贝多芬本人对自己为谁而写毫无疑问。

sentences.en: He said, I don't write for the masses.
sentences.zh: 他说，我不为大众写作。

sentences.en: I write for people who are cultured, like you.
sentences.zh: 我为像你们这样有文化的人写作。

sentences.en: But even though people find his stuff very difficult, they never doubt that Beethoven is a star.
sentences.zh: 但尽管人们觉得他的作品很难，却从未怀疑过贝多芬是一位明星。

sentences.en: And by the 1820s, he really does have a brand.
sentences.zh: 到了19世纪20年代，他确实拥有了一个品牌。

sentences.en: People are painting his portrait.
sentences.zh: 人们在为他画像。

sentences.en: They're making busts of him.
sentences.zh: 他们在为他制作半身像。

sentences.en: Images of Beethoven are going all over Europe, and they're appealing to people who had never really existed before in the history of classical music.
sentences.zh: 贝多芬的形象传遍了整个欧洲，吸引了古典音乐史上从未真正存在过的一类人。

sentences.en: They're not admirers.
sentences.zh: 他们不是仰慕者。

sentences.en: They're not supporters.
sentences.zh: 他们不是支持者。

sentences.en: They're not patrons.
sentences.zh: 他们不是赞助人。

sentences.en: They are fans.
sentences.zh: 他们是粉丝。

sentences.en: And that word is coming from fanatics, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而这个词源于“狂热者”，不是吗？

sentences.en: They're fanatics for Beethoven.
sentences.zh: 他们是贝多芬的狂热者。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And I think part of the reason for this is that Beethoven's image perfectly fits the demands of the times.
sentences.zh: 我认为部分原因在于贝多芬的形象完美契合了时代的需求。

sentences.en: This is a conservative age, an age of reaction.
sentences.zh: 这是一个保守的时代，一个反动的时代。

sentences.en: So people love the idea of tradition.
sentences.zh: 所以人们热爱传统的观念。

sentences.en: They love the idea of Beethoven as the culmination of a tradition that began with Mozart and Haydn.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢把贝多芬视为始于莫扎特和海顿的传统的巅峰。

sentences.en: But what's more, his German-ness is really important.
sentences.zh: 而且更重要的是，他的“德国性”非常重要。

sentences.en: The French Revolution was a foundational moment in the history of German-ness.
sentences.zh: 法国大革命是德国历史上的一个奠基时刻。

sentences.en: That moment when French troops cross the Rhine is when modern German identity is born.
sentences.zh: 当法军越过莱茵河的那一刻，现代德国身份就诞生了。

sentences.en: So people are looking for a German hero.
sentences.zh: 所以人们在寻找一位德国英雄。

sentences.en: And Beethoven perfectly fits the bill.
sentences.zh: 而贝多芬完美地符合这一要求。

sentences.en: But all the time, his health is getting worse.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他的健康状况却在恶化。

sentences.en: By the end of 1826, he's got pneumonia, he's got jaundice, he's got liver issues, and, of course, he can barely hear anything at all.
sentences.zh: 到1826年底，他患上了肺炎、黄疸、肝脏问题，当然，他几乎什么也听不见了。

sentences.en: But apart from that, he's doing fine.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，他状态不错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Apart from that, he's in great form.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，他状态极佳。

sentences.en: Now, we described his final days earlier, the presents and the wine and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 我们之前描述过他最后的日子，礼物、葡萄酒之类的东西。

sentences.en: But, sad to say, on the 26th of March, 1827, in the middle of a tremendous thunderstorm, he takes his final breath.
sentences.zh: 但遗憾的是，1827年3月26日，在一场巨大的雷雨中，他咽下了最后一口气。

sentences.en: And it is said that at the very end, he opens his eyes, he lifts his right hand to heaven, he clenches his fist, and then he collapses.
sentences.zh: 据说在最后时刻，他睁开眼睛，举起右手向天，紧握拳头，然后倒下了。

sentences.en: The artist, defiant to the end.
sentences.zh: 这位艺术家，至死不屈。

sentences.en: So a sad, I want to say, a tragic moment.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个悲伤的，我想说是悲剧性的时刻。

sentences.en: And to mark it, let's now hear, perhaps, the most celebrated thunderstorm in the entire history of classical music.
sentences.zh: 为了纪念这一时刻，让我们来听听古典音乐史上最著名的雷雨。

sentences.en: And it comes from the Sixth Symphony, the Pastoral, and we are going to hear the Fourth Movement, which gives us a thunderstorm, and then, right at the end, the hint of a rainbow.
sentences.zh: 它来自《第六交响曲》（田园），我们将听到第四乐章，它为我们呈现了一场雷雨，然后在最后，出现了一抹彩虹的暗示。

sentences.en: Dominic, we began this half with the funeral of Beethoven, and, lo and behold, we've come full circle.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我们以贝多芬的葬礼开始了这半场节目，瞧，我们又回到了原点。

sentences.en: Exactly, Tom.
sentences.zh: 正是这样，汤姆。

sentences.en: It's almost as if we'd scripted it.
sentences.zh: 简直就像是我们写好剧本一样。

sentences.en: And, as we said before, his death was an extraordinary public occasion.
sentences.zh: 而且，正如我们之前所说，他的葬礼是一场非凡的公共事件。

sentences.en: People were literally queuing up to take snippets of hair from his head to wear in lockets around their necks, like religious relics.
sentences.zh: 人们排着队从他头上剪下一缕头发，像宗教圣物一样戴在脖子上的吊坠里。

sentences.en: Now, there was a very revealing eulogy at the cemetery gates, and it was made by Vienna's greatest playwright, a man called Franz Grillparzer.
sentences.zh: 在墓地大门口有一篇非常发人深省的悼词，是由维也纳最伟大的剧作家弗朗茨·格里尔帕泽发表的。

sentences.en: Tom, are you familiar with his work?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你熟悉他的作品吗？

sentences.en: Um, I'm not...
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不……

sentences.en: I mean, I'll be honest, it sounds like an American steak restaurant rather than a great writer.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这听起来像是一家美国牛排馆，而不是一位伟大的作家。

sentences.en: It doesn't take it.
sentences.zh: 这可不行。

sentences.en: And it doesn't encourage me to want to read it, I have to say.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，这并不能鼓励我想去读他的作品。

sentences.en: Well, Grillparzer, in the eulogy, did not mention God at all.
sentences.zh: 好吧，格里尔帕泽在悼词中根本没有提到上帝。

sentences.en: Extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 非同寻常。

sentences.en: He mentioned only the gods of music and art.
sentences.zh: 他只提到了音乐和艺术之神。

sentences.en: He was an artist, he said of Beethoven.
sentences.zh: 他说贝多芬是一位艺术家。

sentences.en: That's how he spoke again.
sentences.zh: 他又是那样说的。

sentences.en: That's how all Germans speak when they're talking about art, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，所有德国人在谈论艺术时都是这样说话的。

sentences.en: And all that was his was his through art alone.
sentences.zh: 他所拥有的一切，都是通过艺术获得的。

sentences.en: He was an artist, and who shall arise to stand beside him?
sentences.zh: 他是一位艺术家，还有谁能与他并肩而立呢？

sentences.en: Who, indeed?
sentences.zh: 确实，还有谁呢？

sentences.en: And this, I think, was Beethoven's greatest legacy.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是贝多芬最伟大的遗产。

sentences.en: You talked about Mozart as a genius.
sentences.zh: 你谈到莫扎特是一位天才。

sentences.en: I think what Mozart, what Beethoven, rather, creates is the idea of the artist with a capital A, the individual who suffers and overcomes,
sentences.zh: 我认为莫扎特，不，贝多芬所创造的是“艺术家”的概念，大写的“艺术家”，一个受苦并克服苦难的个体，

sentences.en: the martyr, the man who stands alone from the masses, somebody whose work, like mine, is long and difficult,
sentences.zh: 殉道者，一个独立于大众之外的人，一个像我一样作品漫长而艰深的人，

sentences.en: and therefore profound.
sentences.zh: 因此也是深刻的。

sentences.en: Tom, he can see things and hear things that you and I can't.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，他能看到和听到你我无法感知的东西。

sentences.en: Well, he can't actually hear them, can he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他实际上听不见，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that's the whole point.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这正是重点所在。

sentences.en: No, that's true.
sentences.zh: 不，那是真的。

sentences.en: We'll always have that over Beethoven, won't we?
sentences.zh: 我们在这点上总能胜过贝多芬，不是吗？

sentences.en: So let us end with the passage that for many people represents the climax of Beethoven's genius.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们以那段对许多人而言代表了贝多芬天才巅峰的乐章作为结束。

sentences.en: Beethoven began his Ninth Symphony in 1822, and at its heart is Friedrich Schiller's Ode to Joy, which he'd first written in 1785.
sentences.zh: 贝多芬于1822年开始创作他的第九交响曲，其核心是弗里德里希·席勒于1785年创作的《欢乐颂》。

sentences.en: A kind of hymn to enlightenment values.
sentences.zh: 那是一首启蒙价值观的赞歌。

sentences.en: As always, it's a complicated story.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，这是一个复杂的故事。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Schiller was horrified by the excesses of the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 席勒对法国大革命的过激行为感到震惊。

sentences.en: He was horrified by the execution of the king and the terror, and he actually toned down his original Ode to Joy to make it less radical, to make it more conservative.
sentences.zh: 他对国王被处决和恐怖统治感到惊恐，实际上他淡化了最初的《欢乐颂》，使其不那么激进，变得更加保守。

sentences.en: And this is the version that Beethoven used.
sentences.zh: 而这正是贝多芬所使用的版本。

sentences.en: But my favourite story about the Ode to Joy and about the Ninth Symphony is one that many of you will know.
sentences.zh: 但我关于《欢乐颂》和第九交响曲最喜欢的故事，是你们许多人都知道的一个。

sentences.en: Lots of you who know the story of Beethoven will know this story.
sentences.zh: 很多了解贝多芬故事的人都会知道这个故事。

sentences.en: Because when the symphony was first performed in 1824,
sentences.zh: 因为当这部交响曲在1824年首次演出时，

sentences.en: Beethoven stood at the front,
sentences.zh: 贝多芬站在最前面，

sentences.en: waving his arms next to the conductor, even though he could not hear a note.
sentences.zh: 在指挥旁边挥舞着双臂，尽管他一个音符也听不见。

sentences.en: And when it was all over, he couldn't hear the applause behind him.
sentences.zh: 当演出结束时，他听不到身后的掌声。

sentences.en: And very gently, the singer Carolina Unger turned him round so that he could see, but not hear, the standing ovation.
sentences.zh: 然后，歌唱家卡罗琳·昂格非常温柔地将他转过身来，让他能看到，虽然听不到，那全场起立鼓掌的盛况。

sentences.en: Brilliant, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 太棒了，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And we have some ovations of our own to give.
sentences.zh: 我们也有一些掌声要送出。

sentences.en: An ovation to the Royal Albert Hall for hosting us,
sentences.zh: 向主办我们活动的皇家阿尔伯特音乐厅致敬，

sentences.en: to the Academy of St. Martin in the Fields, wonderful, wonderful orchestra, to the Philharmonia Chorus,
sentences.zh: 向圣马丁室内乐团，这支美妙绝伦的乐团，向爱乐合唱团致敬，

sentences.en: its chorus master, Gavin Carr, to our wonderful soloists,
sentences.zh: 向他们的合唱指挥加文·卡尔，向我们出色的独唱家们致敬，

sentences.en: Nardis Williams, Katie Stevenson,
sentences.zh: 纳迪斯·威廉姆斯、凯蒂·史蒂文森，

sentences.en: Andrew Staples, William Thomas,
sentences.zh: 安德鲁·斯台普斯、威廉·托马斯，

sentences.en: Mishka, Rushdie, Momin.
sentences.zh: 米什卡、拉什迪、莫明。

sentences.en: But I think, above all, we owe a debt of thanks to the great guiding spirit behind this entire evening, the man whose idea it was, the wonderful Oliver Zeffman.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，最重要的是，我们必须感谢今晚整个活动的伟大引导者，这个想法的提出者，出色的奥利弗·泽夫曼。

sentences.en: And Tom, let's be honest, it's hard to admit it, but we would be nothing without our own aristocratic sponsors.
sentences.zh: 还有汤姆，说实话，虽然很难承认，但没有我们自己的贵族赞助人，我们什么也不是。

sentences.en: So, a huge thank you to Tony Pasta and Jack Davenport, the Habsburg emperors of our hearts.
sentences.zh: 所以，非常感谢托尼·帕斯塔和杰克·达文波特，我们心中的哈布斯堡皇帝。

sentences.en: Thank you to our Viennese aristocratic patrons, the brilliant Tabby Syrette, and Anoushka Lewis, and to our Parisian friend, the peerless Theo Young-Smith,
sentences.zh: 感谢我们的维也纳贵族赞助人，出色的塔比·赛雷特和阿努什卡·刘易斯，以及我们巴黎的朋友，无与伦比的西奥·杨-史密斯，

sentences.en: and all of their colleagues, a goal-hanger podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 以及他们所有的同事，Goalhanger播客团队。

sentences.en: And, of course, a huge, huge thank you to all of you for coming and for your encouragement with this.
sentences.zh: 当然，还要非常非常感谢你们所有人的到来，以及对我们的鼓励。

sentences.en: I think it's been an amazing evening.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个美妙的夜晚。

sentences.en: It's been a privilege to be sat up here listening to this incredible music.
sentences.zh: 能坐在这里聆听如此美妙的音乐是一种荣幸。

sentences.en: So, thank you.
sentences.zh: 所以，谢谢大家。

sentences.en: And now, to play us out, it's over to Oliver and to Ludwig.
sentences.zh: 现在，让我们以音乐结束，有请奥利弗和路德维希。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: We will be back next week without musical accompaniment.
sentences.zh: 下周我们将回归，不再有音乐伴奏。

sentences.en: And the series coming out next Monday will be on
sentences.zh: 下周一推出的系列节目将是

sentences.en: The Nazis' Road to War.
sentences.zh: 《纳粹的战争之路》。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
